Why does my std::thread pool deadlock when a worker panics?

help concurrency
kestrel Mar 3

I have a small thread pool built on std::sync::mpsc: a shared receiver behind a Mutex, eight workers, and a join that waits for a counter to reach zero. When one job panics, join never returns.

let job = rx.lock().unwrap().recv();
match job {
    Ok(f) => { f(); pending.fetch_sub(1, SeqCst); }
    Err(_) => break,
}

What is the idiomatic way to make the pool survive a panicking job?

quinedot Mar 3 Solution

The panic unwinds out of f() before fetch_sub runs, so the counter never reaches zero. Worse, if the panic happens while the guard from rx.lock() is alive, the mutex is poisoned and every other worker's unwrap() panics too.

Decrement in a drop guard so it runs during unwinding, and catch the panic per job with catch_unwind so the worker thread lives on:

let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(f));
pending.fetch_sub(1, SeqCst);

Also take the job out of the lock before running it, so a panic can never poison the receiver mutex.

kestrel Mar 4

That was it. Moving recv() out of the guard's scope and wrapping the job in catch_unwind fixed the deadlock, and the pool now reports the panic message instead of hanging.
